You are helping a START Hack Munich 2026 team (challenge by Lio: "Keep the Line Running"). Read /Users/akshatkhair/Documents/Projects/ask-soony/AGENTS.md and README.md first for the challenge brief and rules.

All 308 portal files are already downloaded and unzipped under /Users/akshatkhair/Documents/Projects/ask-soony/data/soony-data/ (79 under soony/ = customer context, 229 under suppliers/ = six suppliers' documents). Types: 215 pdf, 44 jpg, 16 png, 25 csv, 7 xlsx, 1 md. Data is deliberately messy: contradictions, missing values, scans, four languages (KR, CN, PL, EN).

Goal: build a thorough understanding of the data so the team can pick a product direction. Read every file (use pdftotext / python with openpyxl or pandas for xlsx/csv; view images with the Read tool, which handles images and PDFs including scans; translate non-English content). Skim similar files in bulk where they are clearly templated, but open enough of each kind to be sure.

Write findings to /Users/akshatkhair/Documents/Projects/ask-soony/data/UNDERSTANDING.md (data/ is gitignored; the data is confidential — never copy it anywhere outside data/, never commit, never send to external services). Cover:
1. File inventory: folder structure, what each group of files is, per supplier.
2. The situation: orders still open (128,000 Standard × 4 parts, 25,200 Collector's × 7 parts), bill of materials, which supplier delivers which part, quantities, delivery schedules, packing capacity/shifts in Hamburg (Sat 06–22, Sun 06–20), deadline Sun 22 Nov 20:00.
3. Gap analysis: where supply, schedule or capacity falls short; the binding constraints; rough numbers.
4. Contradictions, missing values and traps found, each with the files that disagree.
5. Policies/rules (e.g. approval_policy_PP-07) that constrain what an agent may decide or must escalate.
6. Supplier contact facts relevant for agents writing to suppliers (no real secrets).
7. 3–5 candidate product ideas where agents do real work (read, decide, act), ranked, with which data each relies on.
Keep it dense and factual; cite file paths. Do not edit any file outside data/. Return a 10-line summary of the key findings when done.

content.content:
# AGENTS.md

Guidance for coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, others) working in this repo.

## What this is

Our entry for the Lio challenge "Keep the Line Running" at START Hack Munich 2026.

- Fictional customer: Soony, a games publisher launching Grand Heist 6 on Sun 22 Nov, 20:00
- Everything is packed in one distribution center in Hamburg; six suppliers deliver the parts
- Still open at kickoff: 128,000 Standard Editions (4 parts each) and 25,200 numbered Collector's Editions (7 parts each)
- Packing time left: Sat 06:00 to 22:00, Sun 06:00 to 20:00

The product idea is not fixed yet. Check the README and recent commits for the current direction.

## The rules that shape the code

- **Agents do real work.** They read, decide and act: write to suppliers, open decisions, escalate. A dashboard on top of a spreadsheet is not enough.
- **Nothing hardcoded.** Never copy values from the data into code. Everything is derived from the portal data at runtime.
- **The data changes.** New files land in the portal during the hack, unannounced. Code must handle new and changed files without a rebuild.
- **The data is messy on purpose.** Expect contradictions, missing values, scans and four languages (KR, CN, PL, EN). Surface contradictions instead of silently picking one side.
- **Confidential.** Use the data only for this hackathon and never share it outside the team. Do not commit portal data (`data/` is gitignored); fetch it through the API.

## Data access

- Customer portal: `https://start-hack-portal-cxh3crbdaef2f8gt.westeurope-01.azurewebsites.net`
- API (team token from the portal's Settings): `GET /api/v1/files`, `GET /api/v1/files/{path}`, `GET /api/v1/archive.zip`, `GET /api/v1/openapi.json`
- Token and other secrets go in `.env` (gitignored), never in code or commits
- Supplier email only gets answers from sender addresses registered in the portal's Settings

## Deadlines

- **Sun 12:00:** hand-in: deployed prototype, pitch deck, demo video (max 3 min), this repo with a short README
- **Sun 14:00:** live demo, 3 min pitch plus 2 min questions

Prefer working, deployed and demoable over complete. Go deep on one problem.

## Entire (session tracking)

Entire records agent sessions as checkpoints and links them to commits.

- Hooks for Claude Code (`.claude/settings.json`) and Codex (`.codex/hooks.json`) are committed; they do nothing if `entire` is not installed
- Checkpoints upload to this (private) repo on `git push`

### Setup (once per clone)

1. Install the CLI. macOS: `brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire`. Other systems: see https://docs.entire.io/cli/installation
2. Check it runs: `entire --version`
3. In your clone, install the git hooks (they link commits to checkpoints and upload them on push):

   ```bash
   entire enable --agent claude-code --local --telemetry=false
   entire agent add codex    # only if you use Codex
   ```

   `--local` writes your choices to `.entire/settings.local.json`, so the shared `.entire/settings.json` stays unchanged. Drop `--telemetry=false` if you don't mind anonymous usage stats.
4. **Restart your agents:** quit every Claude Code or Codex session that was open in this repo and start a new one. Hooks load when a session starts, so sessions that were already running are not tracked
5. Codex only: in the new session, open `/hooks` and approve the Entire hooks
6. Verify: `entire status` should show `Enabled`, your agents, `Checkpoints sync to: origin` and `Secret scanners · betterleaks, goredact`
7. If `entire enable` changed `.claude/settings.json` or `.codex/hooks.json`, check `git diff` before committing; the committed versions already work for everyone

`entire doctor` diagnoses and fixes stuck sessions.
- Shared redaction settings (PII, betterleaks, goredact) live in `.entire/settings.json`; personal settings go in `.entire/settings.local.json` (gitignored)
- Redaction is best effort: never paste secrets into agent sessions

## Conventions

- Commit subjects in imperative mood, at most 50 characters; details as bullets in the body
- One commit per topic
- Keep secrets, tokens and personal data out of code, fixtures and commit messages

# ask-soony

Our entry for the **Lio challenge "Keep the Line Running"** at START Hack Munich 2026.

Soony, a (fictional) games publisher, launches Grand Heist 6 on **Sunday 22 Nov, 20:00**. Every copy is packed in one distribution center in Hamburg, six suppliers deliver the parts, and the last 20% is not packed yet. Soony's data lives in SAP, spreadsheets, PDFs and scans, in four languages. Soony's head of procurement: "We find out at the dock."

We build agents that read that data, decide what is at risk and act on it before it is too late.

## Status

Work in progress. The product direction is being decided; this README will describe it once it is fixed.

## Getting started

1. Clone the repo
2. Create a `.env` in the repo root with the team token from the portal's Settings:

   ```bash
   SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN=your-team-token
   ```

3. Set up Entire so your agent sessions are tracked: see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#entire-session-tracking)

Run instructions follow once the stack is in place.

## Data

All customer data comes from the Soony portal at runtime (`GET /api/v1/files`, `/api/v1/archive.zip`). It is confidential: use it only for this hackathon, never share it outside the team and never commit it (`data/` is gitignored).

## Hand-in (Sun 12:00)

- [ ] Working prototype, deployed
- [ ] Pitch deck
- [ ] Demo video, max 3 minutes
- [ ] This repo with a short README (how to run, what it does)

Live demo from Sun 14:00: 3 minutes of pitch, 2 minutes of questions.

# Kickoff with Soony – onboarding notes

Date: 2026-11-11
Attendees: Jonas Lindqvist (CPO), Dr. Maren Vogt (Head of Procurement), Raj Patel (Logistics), us

## What they said

- Grand Heist 6 goes on sale on Sunday 22 November 2026 at 20:00. The date is fixed by retail and by 487,000 pre-orders. "Produced" means packed at the distribution center in Hamburg (DC-HAM).
- Two editions. Standard: game card, case, sleeve, leaflet. Collector's: numbered, 72,000 copies, all pre-ordered, with steel case, art book, poster and a statue.
- The developer finished the game master late. Programmed game cards only started arriving three weeks ago, so Hamburg packs until the last hour.
- Since the first game cards arrived it has been crisis mode: buyers chasing suppliers by phone every day, freight rebooked from sea to air and back, every shift packing whatever arrived that day. Maren: "We get through by working around problems, not by solving them. The team is exhausted."
- The last 20 % will have no buffer. Jonas: "One late pallet on launch weekend and fans who paid for a numbered Collector's Edition get nothing."
- Why us: no time for a tender or a big vendor project. They need help now, before the launch, not next quarter. Jonas: "We cannot afford a single surprise in the last days before the launch."
- Six suppliers, and procurement knows them through paper: contracts, order confirmations, delivery notes. Every supplier has its own folder now. "Half of what we know is in a PDF somebody scanned."
- SAP holds the purchase orders, nothing else. There are two exports because the interface changed in mid-2025.
- Maren: suppliers tell them about problems too late. "We find out at the dock."
- Raj: about 20 open shipments, tracked in a shared spreadsheet that is updated when someone remembers.
- Delivery notes are scanned by the receiving team in Hamburg. Receiving books what is on the paper.
- Suppliers write in their own language. Nobody in procurement reads Polish or Korean.
- The Category Lead for Collector's Items left in the summer. The position is open.

## Open questions we did not get to

- What does a missing copy cost on day one? (Maren: "ask me at the booth")
- Who signs off on air freight?
- Which parts have only one source?
- Why does the stock list show no lid magnets?

## Data they gave us

See the portal: one folder per supplier under `suppliers/`, Soony's own data under `soony/`. They warned us: "It is what it is."
